svg.title: How we implement Stage 2: giving data its meaning
svg.desc: Stage 2 takes the user stories and entity sketch from Stage 1 and asks three questions of each observable property of an entity type: what is it about, where and how is it observed, and under which conditions it can be trusted. The answers, classified against 14 semantic capabilities in 4 categories aligned with ISO/IEC 30141:2024, give Stage 3 a spec per property: what to look for in the standards. Worked example: Madrid need L-0015, the lux received in the area of use (a sidewalk or roadway). Where we are: capabilities and rules defined and tested; open questions on the actions and events the sketch records, and on context and requirements; next steps.
svg.text: How we implement Stage 2: giving data its meaning
Semantic Capabilities · Three questions for each property in the entity sketch · 14 capabilities for any city service
an entity type, one at a time
The result people get, what the
infrastructure does, or what it uses
Not observable? Back to the city.
What it is about, how it is observed
and when to trust it: what to look for
The same capabilities apply to lighting, water and any other service.
“Know the effective lighting received in the area of use” · Technician / Operator
Service Outcome: the light people receive, not what the lamp emits
Observation Point: on the sidewalk or roadway
Method: occasional campaigns; instrument not stated
Scope, height and time basis: not stated
Operational Context: the installation's dimming at that moment
Physical Context: “surfaces, positions”; which ones not stated
Source and quality of the reading: not stated
Find a standard that gives lux in the area of use, with the dimming at that moment
Height and scope of the reading · required level, who sets it · the city's question
Rules for each capability, with tie-breakers
Tested: 14 Madrid stories, 2,752 OMA data points (draft)
Actions the sketch records: e.g. dimming a street
Events the sketch records: e.g. a lamp failure
Context and requirements: e.g. trees, backup power
SIG decisions on the open questions
Classify the sketches from Stage 1 small groups
Confirm reuse with the 33 irrigation needs
A value is only useful with its meaning attached: what it is about, where and how it was measured,
and when it can be trusted. Stage 2 makes that meaning explicit, before any standard is chosen.

Smart Cities SIG working analysis, October 2026. Example from the needs collected in workshops with Madrid municipality departments; classification is the SIG's pilot reading, not yet validated with Madrid.
